s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement following vaccination, with a prolonged and worsening course
salient_findings: Fever and erythema on trunk and extremities after vaccination
Elevated inflammatory markers and abnormal laboratory tests
Imaging findings of hepatosplenomegaly, coronary artery occlusion, and thrombi
key_facts: 22-year-old Japanese man with no medical history or family history
Developed fever and erythema 3 days after receiving first dose of Moderna vaccine
Symptoms worsened leading to hospitalization on the 24th day after second vaccination
Initial presentation included fever and erythema on the trunk and extremities
C-reactive protein was elevated at 19.77 mg/dL
Leukocyte count was elevated at 12,480/μL
Serum ferritin was elevated at 443.1 ng/mL
D-dimer was elevated at 1.1 µg/mL
High-sensitivity troponin I was elevated at 6327 pg/mL during readmission
Platelet count decreased from 271 × 10³/μL to 87 × 10³/μL
Imaging studies showed hepatosplenomegaly, coronary artery occlusion, and thrombi
SARS-CoV-2 PCR test results were repeatedly negative

shortlist.label: Kawasaki disease
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement following vaccination, with a prolonged and worsening course, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C)
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Kawasaki disease, with a strong temporal association with vaccination and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic vasculitis with multi-organ involvement, including coronary artery occlusion and thrombi, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation, elevated ferritin, and thrombocytopenia, which are consistent with this rare but life-threatening condition

shortlist.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
shortlist.why_kept: Coronary artery occlusion and thrombi, with a history of recent vaccination, which may be related to this rare vasculitic condition

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, erythema, and elevated inflammatory markers, along with the temporal relationship to COVID-19 vaccination and the multisystem involvement, are consistent with MIS-C. Although the patient is an adult, MIS-C has been reported in adults, and the clinical presentation and laboratory findings align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kawasaki disease
rejected.why: While Kawasaki disease is a consideration, the patient's age and the presence of coronary artery occlusion and thrombi are less typical for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest polyarteritis nodosa, which typically presents with more localized vascular inflammation.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated ferritin and inflammatory markers, the clinical presentation and imaging findings do not strongly support hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

rejected.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest thromboangiitis obliterans, which typically presents with more localized vascular inflammation and thrombosis.
